title: Al Bowlly's arrival in Berlin
summary: Bowlly came to Berlin after a South African orchestra folded; Briggs put him on his recording sessions until he joined Marek Weber at the Adlon, as did Danny Polo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: So what was Danny Polo doing around that time?
And Al Bowlly was just brand new at that time?

Well, you see, Al Bowlly, he came to Berlin with an orchestra, South African orchestra by the name of Adler. And it seems that they folded or something, something happened, and Al used to go, he'd go to Berlin, they folded in Hamburg, or

something.
And he figured, "Well, I'll go to Berlin and see what I can do." And naturally when he came to Berlin, he saw the name, my name, and which he saw was Briggs.
And he came to see me and he told me --
This is an English name. He saw that.

Yes, yes, right.
He came and he said, "Well, things are pretty rough for the time being, if --
I said, "There's no point," I said, "I've got some recording sessions, and you'll be on all of them."

So, until he found work, he contacted Marek Weber who was at the Adler Hotel, and had a very fine, what you would call, "society orchestra," and vocalist, a nice vocalist who fitted nicely with him, you see, and he worked with them.

He was working full-time with that band, wasn't he?
